key_insight: On-policy distillation (OPD) changes model parameters in a surprisingly small and coordinate-sparse way, even though it uses dense teacher supervision. The updates are spread across layers and tend to concentrate in feed-forward network components, revealing a clear geometry behind how OPD works.
problem_solved: This paper tackles the lack of understanding around how on-policy distillation modifies model parameters. It aims to explain the sparsity and structure of OPD updates across language and vision-language models.
method: Analyze OPD-style post-training updates across multiple language and vision-language model pairs.
Measure how parameter changes are distributed across layers and coordinates during student training on on-policy trajectories.
Study the geometry of the update patterns to identify where and how dense supervision translates into sparse parameter movement.
impact: For practitioners, this helps explain why OPD can be effective despite making only small updates to the model. It can guide better distillation design, debugging, and efficiency-focused post-training choices.
visual_elements: Layer-wise heatmap of update magnitudes showing sparse, distributed changes
Bar chart comparing dense teacher supervision vs. sparse parameter updates
Model diagram highlighting FFN layers as major update hotspots
Trajectory-to-update pipeline illustration for on-policy distillation
paper_title: Dense Supervision, Sparse Updates: On the Sparsity and Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
paper_authors: Guo Yu, Wenlin Liu, Yulan Hu, Hao-Xuan Ma, Jun-Peng Jiang
